value.body: A robotics engineer builds and programs robots — industrial arms on assembly lines, mobile robots in warehouses, or robots in research and products. Employers include factory-automation integrators, robot makers, manufacturers, warehouse-automation firms and start-ups. Work mixes programming, mechanical and electrical integration, and testing in the lab or at a customer site.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Mechatronics, Mechanical, Electrical or Electronics

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Robot teach pendants, ROS, PLCs, Python / C++, CAD

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as application or commissioning engineers at automation integrators, working on robot cells in factories. Projects with ROS or microcontrollers and robotics competitions help; research and autonomy roles often expect an M.Tech or MS.

value.title: At a glance
items: Commissioning roles can involve long stretches at customer sites.
Industrial robot work and research robotics are quite different jobs.
Next roles: senior robotics engineer, automation project lead, controls specialist.
